title: API Error Handling
summary: Design predictable error contracts for expected failures without leaking unexpected exception details.
objectives: Distinguish expected application errors from unexpected failures.
Explain the role of Problem Details and stable machine-readable codes.
Avoid exposing implementation details or private data in API errors.

sections.heading: Errors are part of the contract

reviewCandidates.prompt: How do expected API errors differ from unexpected failures?
reviewCandidates.answer: Expected errors represent known outcomes such as invalid input or a stale edit, with intentional client actions. Unexpected failures need a safe generic server-error response and diagnostics.

reviewCandidates.prompt: Why should an API avoid returning raw exception details to clients?
reviewCandidates.answer: They can expose stack traces, internal structure or sensitive data. A safe error contract and correlation ID support clients without leaking those details.

reviewCandidates.prompt: Why are stable machine-readable error codes useful alongside HTTP status codes?
reviewCandidates.answer: Status codes classify broad outcomes, while stable application codes distinguish actionable causes without requiring clients to parse changing human messages.
